# Plink Piano

> Plink Piano: Practice Tracker is an iPhone and iPad app (coming soon to the App Store) that logs piano practice by itself. Connect a digital piano over USB or Bluetooth MIDI and play: Plink records practice time and streaks, recognises the pieces you play from the notes, and shows where you stumble. No account, no servers, works offline; data stays on the user's devices and their own iCloud.

## Guides

- [How to connect a Roland FP-30X to an iPhone or iPad](https://kiracih.github.io/plink-website/guides/connect-roland-fp-30x-iphone.html): USB cable or Bluetooth MIDI paired inside the app, and troubleshooting.
- [How to track piano practice automatically](https://kiracih.github.io/plink-website/guides/track-piano-practice-automatically.html): manual journals, lesson apps, recorder boxes and MIDI apps compared.
- [Roland Piano App vs Plink: can you use both?](https://kiracih.github.io/plink-website/guides/roland-piano-app-and-plink.html): what each does; both can share one Bluetooth connection on the same iPhone (tested on an FP-30X).
- [Yamaha Smart Pianist vs Plink: can you use both?](https://kiracih.github.io/plink-website/guides/yamaha-smart-pianist-and-plink.html): what each does; how to connect both on Yamaha pianos.
- [Kawai PianoRemote vs Plink: can you use both?](https://kiracih.github.io/plink-website/guides/kawai-pianoremote-and-plink.html): what each does; one Bluetooth device per piano; apps on that device share it.
- [Using forScore with a digital piano and a practice tracker](https://kiracih.github.io/plink-website/guides/forscore-and-plink.html): forScore counts time a score is open, Plink counts playing; one Bluetooth device per piano, so a second device uses USB.
